newsitem.title: FINLAND: ETLA SEES EMU START ON TIME, LENIENCY ON CRITERIA.
newsitem.headline: ETLA SEES EMU START ON TIME, LENIENCY ON CRITERIA.

text.p: The likelihood that the third stage of European economic and monetary union will start on time is high and the entry criteria may be interpreted with leniency, a Finnish economic think-tank said on Wednesdsay.
"The likelihood that the EMU will be formed in the beginning of 1999 is high," the Research Institute of the Finnish Economy (ETLA) said in a statement.

"The difficulties of Germany and France in fulfilling the criteria are one factor creating uncertainty. The criteria may, if necessary, be interpreted leniently enough that this does not pose a barrier to the formation of EMU," it said.
Major EU member countries and the EU commission were committed to EMU, ETLA noted.
Finland would "easily fulfil" the single currency convergence criteria on public sector debt and deficit this year, the institute said.

ETLA's 1997 EMU-deficit forecast for Finland at 1.5 percent of gross domestic product was even more optimistic than the finance ministry's February 18 forecast of 1.9 percent, despite a lower 1997 GDP growth forecast -- four percent compared to the ministry's 4.6 percent.
"It is possible, even likely, that the ERM central rate will become the rate at which the markka will be irrevocably pegged to the euro in the beginning of 1999," ETLA said.
The markka was linked to Europe's exchange rate mechanism (ERM) in October 1996 at a central parity rate of 3.04 per German mark. --Helsinki newsroom +358-9-680 50 245, e-mail news@reuters.fi
